mt: 'ARQUIVO PESSOA' ON THE OVERVIEW — THE EDITION OF THE PUBLISHED WORK AT ITS GRAIN; THE ORTHONYM'S POETRY DROPPED FROM ITS LIST; THE PSEUDONYMS AND THE JOINT ATTRIBUTIONS NOT CARRIED; THE EDITION CREDITED TO A PARTNER
d: THE EDITION, SIGNED OUT, 2026-11-01: 'The Arquivo Pessoa is a digital library and database dedicated to the published work of the Portuguese writer Fernando Pessoa.' Key details: arquivopessoa.net; origin ('Created between 1997 and 2008 by the Institute of Studies into Modernism at Lisbon's Universidade Nova, directed by Leonor Areal, and evolved from an earlier 1997 multimedia CD-ROM'); contents ('Pessoa’s poetry, prose, heteronyms, and orthonyms'), five categories listed; features (search, the 'Labirinto' with 'audio readings and images'). Three cards: the edition's home and Info pages, Art and Soul Group. The paste ends on the third card.
reading: The innocent reading first. Asked for the archive, the Overview says what it holds, where it is, who made it and when, lists its main sections and describes its tools.
findings: THE SECTIONS, ONE DROPPED. The home-page card: '1. Poemas de Alberto Caeiro 2. Poesia de Álvaro de Campos 3. Odes de Ricardo Reis 4. Poesia Ortónima de Fernando Pessoa 5. Livro do Desa...'. The composition lists Caeiro, Campos, Reis, 'Livro do Desassossego' and 'Mensagem': the fourth section, the orthonym's poetry, falls out, and the orthonym stays in the list only through Mensagem, a title the list does not attribute.

THE CLASSES OF NAME. 'Pessoa’s poetry, prose, heteronyms, and orthonyms'. The author index: 'Ortónimo, pseudónimos e heterónimos de Fernando Pessoa', one orthonym, then the pseudonyms and heteronyms, 39 names in all. The composition puts the orthonym in the plural and does not carry the pseudonyms, the third class; the joint attributions the index keeps ('Álvaro de Campos e Ricardo Reis', 'Wardour + Pessoa', 'A. L. Caeiro e J. Caeiro') are absent. The census row reads the index as the work held under the names it bears, answerable to one name, 'Obra de Fernando Pessoa'; the composition gives the heteronyms as contents of a corpus.

THE EDITION CREDITED TO A PARTNER. 'Created between 1997 and 2008 by the Institute of Studies into Modernism at Lisbon's Universidade Nova, directed by Leonor Areal'. The edition's own technical sheet: 'Edição: Obra Aberta CRL, 2008', 'Concepção e direcção: Leonor Areal', with the Instituto de Estudos sobre o Modernismo under 'Parcerias'. The composition's wording follows the Art and Soul card ('Between 1997 and 2008 the Institute of Studies into Modernism at Lisbon´s Universidade Nova created this very useful website'); Obra Aberta is unnamed, and the 1997 CD-ROM stands without its publishers ('Edição original: Texto Editora e Casa Fernando Pessoa, 1997').

THE VOICES NOT CARRIED. 'the "Labirinto" (which features audio readings and images)'. The technical sheet gives each of four names its own reader: 'Alberto Pimenta (Ricardo Reis) José Abreu (Alberto Caeiro) José Lopes (Álvaro de Campos) Teresa Faria (Fernando Pessoa)'. The composition gives the readings without the names they voice.
analysis: An accurate composition of the edition's scope and sections that thins its division of names: the orthonym's poetry drops from the list, the pseudonyms and joint attributions are absent, and the editor is replaced by a partner named on a third-party card.
per_note: Leonor Areal and the Institute named, the editor Obra Aberta not; the edition's pages and one third-party page carded.
